instruction: Turn off the system sound on my desktop entirely.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: pactl list sinks | grep 'Mute:' | head -n 1 | awk '{print $2}'

metadata.explanation: Task requires muting the system sound. Evaluator uses existing exact_match metric with vm_command_line getter to check PulseAudio mute status is 'yes\n'. Removed 'pulseaudio --start' to avoid restarting PulseAudio during evaluation. Checks actual mute toggle state (not volume level) since mute and volume are separate in PulseAudio. No custom functions needed - reusing official evaluator components.

llm_judge_reasons: Correct verification approach: Command checks PulseAudio mute status using 'pactl list sinks | grep "Mute:"' which correctly verifies the mute toggle state, not volume level.
Proper data extraction: Uses awk to extract the mute status value (yes/no) and compares against expected 'yes\n', which is the correct format for muted audio.
Semantic match with instruction: Instruction says 'mute the system sound completely' and evaluator verifies mute=yes, directly addressing the requirement.
Minor consideration: Checks only the first sink (head -n 1), which is appropriate for most desktop systems where the first sink is typically the default audio output.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional enhancement: Could check all sinks instead of just the first one by removing 'head -n 1' and verifying all outputs are 'yes', though this may be overly strict for typical desktop use cases.
